referents.why: 'brace yourself' / 'your loins': second person of a command in the LORD's speech; the addressee is Job.
'I will question you': second person inside the LORD's speech is the addressee, Job.
'make known to me': first person inside the LORD's speech is the speaker, the LORD (masc sing, named in 38:1).
The implied subject of the command 'gird up' is the one commanded, Job (second masc sing).
The implied 'I' of 'I will question you' is the LORD, the speaker. The builder's self-reference is replaced.
referents.category: implied first person in the speech

referents.why: The implied subject of the command 'make known' is the one told to inform, Job.

links.why: A command joined by waw to a yiqtol in a different person is 'so that' (the and type's own rule), so the plain 'and' is replaced by purpose.
Brace yourself, so that I will question you: a command, then waw + yiqtol in another person looks forward (purpose form 1).
'I will question you, and you shall inform me': a non-command joined by waw to an imperative; not a purpose, so a plain and.

groups.why: The imperative group's roles are command, aim and the rest; 'part' is not a role of an imperative. The 'I will question you' clause is the aim of bracing oneself.
The sender was a slot id; sender and addressee must be candidate ids. The LORD asks, and Job is addressed.
groups.category: turn sender and addressee as candidates

cant_tell.what: The content of 'I will ask you' (the questions) begins in 38:4 and is not linked here
cant_tell.why: The questions are judged with their own verses; here the turn's part is only cl2.
